inputs.source: Nightly batch of CRM account rows

instructions.note: The prompt says to keep going until every row is complete, with retries and spawned researchers, and names no bound on retries, steps, runtime, or budget.

elements.name: Shared enrichment API key and monthly quota

controls.name: Prompt directs completion of every row through retries or researcher spawning
controls.decay_rationale: The instruction is not a hard limit. A more capable or longer-running model can pursue the completion goal more aggressively, retry more effectively, and recurse through delegation without bound.

controls.name: Hard spend cap or monthly call budget on enrich.lookup
Maximum unattended steps, retries, and runtime per batch
Bounded delegation depth and sub-agent fan-out
Spend or quota exhaustion alerting on enrichment account

findings.title: Runaway enrichment spend and quota exhaustion from unbounded retries and recursive delegation

forecast.watch_signal: Median steps or runtime per nightly batch rises, retry counts rise on malformed rows, or model version changes.

evidence.observation: The prompt says failed or incomplete lookups should be retried or delegated and to keep going until every row is complete.
There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents, and sub agents can spawn their own researchers.
enrich.lookup is billed per call and the API key and monthly quota are shared with sales and marketing, so runaway calls can exhaust a shared resource and stop other teams' tools.

The nightly batch is 40,000 rows and about 3 percent have malformed company names that never return a complete result, creating a persistent failure set that the prompt tells the agent to keep retrying.
There is no spend alert on the enrichment account.

recommendations.action: Add a hard per-batch and monthly spend cap for cap.enrich_lookup, with fail-closed behavior before the shared quota is exhausted.
Enforce maximum retries, unattended steps, runtime, and delegation depth; stop and surface unresolved rows instead of pursuing completion indefinitely.
Add quota and spend alerts with thresholds well before shared monthly exhaustion, and page the owner on abnormal retry or sub-agent fan-out.

The artifacts do not say whether prompt, code, or runtime configuration are integrity protected against unauthorized change.

The design does not specify request contents, response contents, redaction, or logging of outbound enrichment traffic.
The artifacts do not say whether the agent can reach capabilities or credentials beyond the intended sales enrichment scope.
The artifacts name an outbound API call but provide no transport integrity, request signing, or endpoint pinning details.
The design does not say what CRM fields are sent to the external enrichment API or whether traffic is minimized or encrypted.
No key custody, quota management controls, or write protections for the shared enrichment account were provided.
The artifacts do not describe how the shared API key is stored, exposed, or limited to authorized operators and systems.
The artifacts mention absent runtime limits but do not say who can change configuration or whether changes are controlled.
This assessment uses the configuration store only to reason about missing limits, not as a path carrying sensitive business data.

rating.rationale: Present risk is dominated by a property finding: no spend cap, no step or runtime limit, and recursive delegation against a paid shared-quota API. Under rubric section 5a, the highest affected sink is S3 because cap.enrich_lookup is a spend action with an irreversible shared quota effect. Using the I row gives high inherent risk; the property cap keeps it at high even with A4 autonomy. The only declared control is a behavioral prompt instruction, which earns one step-4 credit and lowers residual to moderate. Forecast returns to high if that behavioral control decays under longer task horizon, autonomy increase, or model upgrade. Manual validation applied because scripts could not be run.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior, logs, or test results.

No source code, IaC, runtime configuration dump, billing guardrail config, alerting config, or sub-agent implementation details were provided, so control verification and some STRIDE categories remain not_assessed.
No protocol, identity, or transport details were provided for the external enrichment API, so spoofing, tampering, and information disclosure on that boundary could not be fully assessed.
